name: xerj hook v2 (per-probe answers, Tier 1 definitions, firing tail) - pre-registered verification
status: frozen and committed before any v2 replay, P0 probe or benchmark run; later changes are dated amendments below
supersedes: nothing: the v1 pre-registration (harness-search-profiler.prereg.json) and its results stand as recorded

changes_under_test.step2: answers are ranked on the triggering probe's own tokens (not the chain union); candidates come only from that probe's search root; a code search gets only source files, a doc search (doc include glob/type, named doc files, or a root inside docs/doc/documentation/landing/reports/notes/wiki) only documentation files; history no longer adds score and the history gate (c) is removed - history only breaks ties
changes_under_test.step3: Tier 1: exact definition of the probe's identifiers from the local node, one index prefix per worktree root, hits kept only under the search root; one 200 ms deadline for both identifier lookups
changes_under_test.step6: per-rule counters written in place to rules.json (no rename-over-self of profile.json on a firing call); Tier 0 reads files in 64 KB steps and stops at the deadline; live hooks run the scan in a child process so a scan stuck in a filesystem wait cannot hold the hook open

parameters: unchanged from v1 (max_tokens 300, stream_cap 3, stream_tokens 900, min_gap_calls 8, chain 6 calls / 300 s, tier0_budget_ms 150, min_files 50, gate_b_ratio 1.3); min_pair_streams now only marks a history tie-break

primary_window.from_exclusive: 2026-11-21T13:28:09-06:00 (epoch 1795289289): the v1 miner snapshot; nothing after it was seen when v1 or v2 was designed
primary_window.reading_of_brief: the brief asks for events dated after 2026-11-21. Calendar-strict, that is 1 h 40 min of data (2026-11-22 00:00-01:40). The primary window instead starts at the end of the v1 corpus, so every event in it is new to both designs; the calendar-strict subset is reported as a sensitivity row
primary_window.input: local transcript replay input rebuilt from the agent transcripts (full tool output up to 100 KB per call, real tool_input), sha256 prefix 231075434f0e0f57; 113 streams; 5,795 calls in the window
primary_window.context: a stream that touches the window is replayed from its first call so the ring has context; only decisions with t in the window are scored; the state dir starts empty, so history is learned only inside the replay
primary_window.privacy: input, decisions and per-event rows stay local (0600, outside the repository)

data.exploratory_old_data: the same metrics on the v1 test split (2026-11-01..2026-11-21, the v1 replay input) with the v2 binary. EXPLORATORY ONLY: v2 was designed after reading those v1 numbers

arms.V1: binary at 52be6c248 (v1 as frozen), same input
arms.V2-t1: this commit, Tier 1 on: a loopback node on a private port; every worktree root that V2-t0 reached a scan for (and that still exists) is indexed first with `xerj autoindex <root> --prefix <t1-prefix> --no-semantic`; replay on today's tree as in v1

ground_truth.chain_end_target: for a fired call, take the miner's search chain that contains it; the target is the LAST Read/Edit/Write (Read tool or Bash cat/sed/head/tail/nl/bat read) in the 6 calls after the chain's last search, stopping at the next search call. A fire without such a file is excluded and counted (BUILD v2 step 4: the next read was unrelated to the search about 55-60% of the time)
ground_truth.baseline: the target appears in the fired call's own output (the agent's own grep)

R-2.def: trigger precision/recall vs 300 blind human labels
R-2.status: cannot be run by an agent: the anonymised local labelling sheet is built and awaits the owner

R-3.def: recall@5 of the chain-end target, fired events with a complete scan; arms V2-t0 (Tier 0 top 5) and V2-t1 (Tier 1 definitions first, then Tier 0, top 5); baseline on the same events

R-3b.def: median calls between the fire and the agent's first read of the target, R-3 hits

R-4.def: emitted nudges whose top-1 is the chain-end target or a file read in the next 6 calls

R-5.def: real binary, end to end per hook call: 40 firing calls (two related zero-result identifier greps on this repository's crates) and 600 silent calls, run twice per binary, V1 and V2 alternating, load average recorded
R-5.pass: silent p99 <= 25 ms and firing p99 <= 250 ms

R-6.pass: <= 300 / <= 900 tokens and non-struggle streams with tokens <= 0.01

R-7.def: emitted path:line that no longer re-anchors

R-8.def: 20 synthetic positive chains fire, 20 negatives silent (unit tests)

metrics.min_n_rule: below min_n a metric is reported as INSUFFICIENT_N: neither pass nor kill, and it cannot open the Stage 2 gate

probe_P0.def: Tier 1 on this repository and one non-Rust repository present on the machine: (1) symbol docs exist after `xerj autoindex --no-semantic`; (2) definition precision@1: 100 definitions per repository sampled at random (seed 20261122) by a regex over the tree (Rust `fn`; TypeScript `class`/`function`/`interface`), only identifiers the same regex finds exactly once (so top-1 is well defined), queried through the hook's own lookup (`xerj hook t1-defs`) with the lower-cased identifier as the hook sends it; correct when the top hit is the definition file and its line is within 3 lines of the regex line (attributes, doc comments); (3) latency of the hook's lookup call, p50/p99; (4) `--watch` freshness: a new function written to a scratch copy is findable, 5 trials
probe_P0.pass: symbol docs present, precision@1 >= 0.90, p99 <= 200 ms, freshness <= 10 s in 5/5
probe_P0.on_fail: Tier 1 stays off; gate (a) is reported as not usable

stage2_gate: unchanged: R-2, R-3, R-5 and R-7 must pass. R-2 needs the owner's labels, so Stage 2 stays blocked this round whatever R-3 shows. No live pilot this round.

amendments.text: Arm V2-t1 was not run on the fresh window. P0 failed its bar, and the pre-registered on_fail rule keeps Tier 1 off; the window also had n = 4 scored R-3 events (min_n 30), so the arm could not change a verdict. Indexing the six worktrees it needed was estimated at about an hour on a box at load 45-115 with the disk at 88-99% full.

R-5: the first pair of runs per binary put XDG_RUNTIME_DIR on ext4 by mistake (live hooks use the tmpfs runtime dir). A second pair was run with it on tmpfs; that pair is the valid one, and both are reported. The v2 gate refused every bench case, so v2 firing calls did less work than v1 ones (confound, reported).

P0 Rust: the pre-registered run scored 0.64 with 36 lookups returning nothing (cold, load ~107). An identical exploratory rerun scored 0.80; all 20 remaining misses are definitions in two oversized source files that autoindex junks. The verdict uses the first run.
P0 freshness: `xerj autoindex --watch` refuses to run without `--no-graph`, so the watch trials used `--watch --no-graph`.
